biological.citation: Mutations in ACTL6B Cause Neurodevelopmental Deficits and Epilepsy and Lead to Loss of Dendrites in Human Neurons (PMID: 31031012)
biological.summary: Engineered knockout of ACTL6B in wild-type human neurons caused profound deficits in dendrite development, recapitulated in neurons from individuals with bi-allelic mutations and reversed by clonal genetic repair or exogenous ACTL6B expression. Whole-transcriptome and genomic profiling showed increased BAF complex binding in ACTL6B mutants with transcriptional changes in cytoskeletal genes TPPP and FSCN1. Bi-allelic mutations mimicked deletion deficits (loss-of-function) while heterozygous de novo mutations did not, indicating gain-of-function for the latter.

biological.citation: An epilepsy-associated ACTL6B variant captures neuronal hyperexcitability in a human induced pluripotent stem cell model (PMID: 33141462)
biological.summary: iPSC-derived neurons from EIEE-76 patients carrying ACTL6B p.(Val421_Cys425del) showed impaired ACTL6B protein accumulation due to reduced protein stability. Patient neurons exhibited dysregulated nBAF target gene expression and elevated electrophysiological activity on multielectrode arrays, consistent with the epileptic encephalopathy phenotype. This validated a human iPSC model for EIEE-76 and demonstrated how reduced ACTL6B expression affects neuronal function.

biological.citation: Loss of the neural-specific BAF subunit ACTL6B relieves repression of early response genes and causes recessive autism (PMID: 32312822)
biological.summary: Loss-of-function mutations in ACTL6B (BAF53b), the most significantly mutated gene in the Simons Recessive Autism Cohort, caused recessive ASD in humans and mice. Actl6b knockout mice showed ASD-related behaviors including social and memory impairments, repetitive behaviors, and hyperactivity, and humans/mice lacking ACTL6B had corpus callosum hypoplasia. Mechanistically, ACTL6B loss relieved repression of early response genes including AP1 transcription factors (Fos, Fosl2, Fosb, Junb) and increased chromatin accessibility at AP1 binding sites.
biological.sample_size: 6 families with recessive autism; two mouse genetic backgrounds

biological.citation: MicroRNA-mediated switching of chromatin-remodelling complexes in neural development (PMID: 19561591)
biological.summary: ACTL6B (BAF53b) is a neuron-specific subunit of the nBAF chromatin remodeling complex that replaces BAF53a (ACTL6a) upon mitotic exit in post-mitotic neurons, a switch mediated by miR-9* and miR-124. The nBAF complex containing ACTL6B is essential for an evolutionarily conserved program of post-mitotic neural development and dendritic morphogenesis. Mutation of miR-9*/miR-124 binding sites in BAF53a led to persistent BAF53a expression and defective activity-dependent dendritic outgrowth.

biological.citation: Loss of the neural-specific BAF subunit ACTL6B relieves repression of early response genes and causes recessive autism (PMID: 32312822)
biological.summary: Patient mutations in ACTL6B destabilized the protein in neurons and rerouted dendrites to the wrong glomerulus in the Drosophila olfactory system, demonstrating a conserved role for ACTL6B in neural connectivity across species.

biological.citation: Expression profiling of cell-intrinsic regulators in the process of differentiation of human iPSCs into retinal lineages (PMID: 29751772)
biological.summary: ACTL6B, encoding a component of the SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complex, showed markedly contrasted expression that discriminated hiPSC-derived optic vesicle/retinal ganglion cell lineages from retinal pigment epithelium lineages. This differential expression pattern identified ACTL6B as a lineage-specific biomarker during retinal differentiation from hiPSCs.

biological.citation: The SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complex subunit BAF53B as an immunohistochemical marker for neuroendocrine neoplasms (PMID: 40946270)
biological.summary: BAF53B (ACTL6B) protein was highly expressed in neuroendocrine neoplasm (NEN)-derived cell lines and showed positive immunohistochemical staining in the majority of NEN tissue types tested (SCLC 73.7%, lung carcinoid 75%, medullary thyroid carcinoma 88.9%, neuroblastoma 90%, pheochromocytoma 66.7%), while few non-NEN tumors were positive. BAF53B knockdown in NCI-H889 cells did not affect viability but gene expression microarray suggested BAF53B-regulated genes are associated with NEN development and progression.

biological.citation: SWI/SNF complex heterogeneity is related to polyphenotypic differentiation, prognosis, and immune response in rhabdoid tumors (PMID: 31912158)
biological.summary: ACTL6A and ACTL6B were expressed in a mutually exclusive manner in the developing cerebellum and kidney, but a subset of extra-CNS rhabdoid tumors lost this mutual exclusivity and co-expressed both subunits, correlating with aberrant DNA methylation of neuronal/renal developmental genes and immunohistochemical evidence of neuronal differentiation. This suggests ACTL6B expression is normally restricted to neural lineages and its dysregulation contributes to aberrant differentiation in rhabdoid tumors.

biological.citation: ASHG 2016 - Effectively modeling rare neurodevelopmental disorders: A pilot project identifying a novel chromatin remodelling disease
biological.summary: A novel variant in ACTL6B was identified by exome sequencing in a family with two children with severe seizures and developmental delay. iPSC-derived cortical neural progenitor cells from affected patients showed significantly reduced ACTL6B expression correlating with dysregulation of neuronal differentiation, representing the first description of a disease-causing variant in ACTL6B.

biological.citation: Gene Expression Profiles of Main Olfactory Epithelium in Adenylyl Cyclase 3 Knockout Mice (PMID: 26633363)
biological.summary: Actl6b was significantly downregulated in the main olfactory epithelium of AC3 knockout mice compared to wild-type, identified among genes specifically expressed in mature olfactory neurons. This finding places ACTL6B among genes regulated downstream of adenylyl cyclase 3 signaling in the olfactory system.
biological.significance: greater than 2-fold change; verified by qRT-PCR
